title: Influence of laser chirp and interferometer delay and imbalance on the performance of a time-bin BB84 quantum key distribution system
authors: Loïc Millet, Alberto Boaron, Rob Thew, Gianluca Boso
abstract: We investigate the effect of interferometer delay and imbalance on the performance of a BB84 time-bin quantum key distribution system. We simulate the impact of interference visibility on system performance and measure the visibility of a pair of interferometers as a function of their relative time delay and intensity imbalance. In addition, our analysis highlights the effect of laser chirp on system performance.
summary: This paper analyzes the limitations imposed by optical imperfections—specifically laser chirp, interferometer delay, and imbalance—on time-bin BB84 QKD systems. By simulating and measuring visibility degradation, the authors quantify how these factors reduce the achievable Secret Key Rate. The work is important for developing robust quantum communication hardware by providing concrete metrics for required component stabilization.
main_problem: The study investigates how imperfections like interferometer delay, imbalance, and laser chirp degrade the performance of a time-bin BB84 quantum key distribution (QKD) system.
main_result: System visibility is highly sensitive to these parameters; specifically, laser chirp introduces significant degradation in the Secret Key Rate that must be accounted for beyond simple visibility loss calculations.
method: The authors combine simulations of QKD performance with experimental measurements using advanced techniques like PROUD (ultrafast optical differentiation) to characterize the chirp.
model_or_system: The physical system is a time-bin BB84 QKD protocol implemented using an imbalanced interferometer setup. The analysis models pulse propagation and interference visibility under varying delay, imbalance, and frequency chirp.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), Interference Visibility (V), Intensity Imbalance (U), and the Chirp parameter ($\Delta\omega$ or $ eta$).
important_parameters: System visibility ($V$), relative time delay ($	au$), intensity imbalance, and chirp coefficient ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that linear chirp is the dominant source of phase variation; discrepancies between simulated unchirped results and experimental data are used to quantify the chirp effect.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate SKR vs. visibility (Fig. 1), setup schematics for visibility measurement (Fig. 2) and chirp retrieval (Fig. 4), and contour plots showing visibility dependence on imbalance/delay (Fig. 3, Fig. 6).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the QKD performance metric (SKR vs. V), then measuring how delay and imbalance affect V, and finally introducing chirp analysis using PROUD to quantify an additional, significant degradation factor.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges fundamental quantum optics characterization (chirp measurement) directly into the practical performance limits of a quantum communication protocol (QKD), which is crucial for building real-world quantum networks.
